244083383_cc3567f1.text: These noradrenergic neurons have been shown to be derived from rhombomeres 1-5 in the developing mouse brain (Robertson et al., 2013)

244083383_2348018a.text: in mammals, with one known exception (Imam et al., 2018), the noradrenergic neurons of the locus coeruleus complex are found within the periventricular grey matter and the parvicellular reticular nucleus of the rostral hindbrain

244083383_109c0b30.text: the locus coeruleus complex is comprised of several nuclei

244083383_88c4d5a5.text: Descriptions of the nuclear parcellation of the locus coeruleus complex have been provided in approximately 80 mammal species spanning the phylogenetic breadth of this class. Within the mammalian rostral hindbrain, noradrenergic neurons (revealed with tyrosine hydroxylase and dopamine-ß-hydroxylase immunohistochemistry) have been observed within the periventricular grey matter (A4 and A6 nuclei) and parvicellular reticular nucleus (A5 and A7 nuclei)

244083383_6fd7d5a0.text: In most mammals, the A6 is comprised of a moderate density of neurons, but in Murid rodents, primates, and megachiropteran bats, the A6 exhibits a very high density of neurons.
